cleanIntro: The BANISH COMP 6.5 is a welded, tubeless precision-rifle suppressor sold in stainless (SS) and titanium (TI). BANISH prints a book for each, and the cleaning, disassembly and end cap pages are the same but for the name. It carries either a two-port brake or a flat end cap at the muzzle. The tube is welded and the baffles do not come out: only the mount interface, the brake and the flat end cap can be removed. The service is those parts off, a 24-hour soak, a brass brush in the blast chamber and a thorough clean of every thread, every 50 to 100 rounds. Everything about unloading your rifle comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Rifle unloaded, action open and visibly clear
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the rifle and open the action so you can see there is no ammunition in it. BANISH does not print a clearing procedure for your rifle. It sends you to that gun's own manual, a licensed dealer or the gun's maker if you are not sure how.
steps.prose: Both hands are about to be near the muzzle. An open action you have looked into is what makes that safe.
steps.quote: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.

steps.title: What it is rated for: .22 Creedmoor through 6.5 PRC
steps.action: Check what the can has been fed. BANISH rates it for centerfire cartridges from .22 Creedmoor through 6.5 PRC, and recommends against solid lead or plated lead bullets.
steps.prose: Threads that fit do not make a cartridge suitable. If it has been fired with something outside that range, call BANISH before you fire it again.
steps.aside: Compatible with centerfire cartridges up to 6.5 PRC
steps.quote: The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: The can may still be hot after firing. Wait for it to cool, or use a suppressor cover or gloves, before you take hold of it.
steps.prose: Grabbing a hot can and twisting is how people get burned, and how a joint gets rushed.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use a suppressor cover (sold separately) or gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Hot after firing. Cover or gloves.

steps.title: Take the suppressor off the rifle
steps.action: With the rifle clear and the can cool, take the suppressor off. With the direct-thread mount it unscrews from the barrel threads; it was only hand tightened, so it should come loose by hand. On a quick-detach mount, follow the instructions of whoever made that mount.
steps.prose: BANISH prints how the can goes on and does not print a separate removal sequence. If it will not come off by hand, stop and call BANISH rather than put a tool on the tube.
steps.aside: Hand tighten suppressor only. Once snug, it is ready for use.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, ensure the firearm is unloaded and remove the suppressor.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: ⛔ Mount, brake and end cap only — the baffles stay in
steps.action: The mount interface, the suppressor brake and the flat end cap are the only parts of the COMP 6.5 that can be removed for cleaning. The tube is welded, it is not designed to be fully disassembled, and the baffles cannot come out. There is nothing past those parts for you to open.
steps.prose: The titanium book says the same of the COMP 6.5 TI. Anyone telling you to open either one further is describing a different can.
steps.quote: The welded-tubeless BANISH COMP 6.5 SS is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface, suppressor brake, and flat end cap can be removed for cleaning.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

no.q: The welded-tubeless BANISH COMP 6.5 SS is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface, suppressor brake, and flat end cap can be removed for cleaning.

steps.title: If the flat end cap is fitted: take it off
steps.action: Put the tool key supplied with the can on a T-45 Torx wrench, fit the key to the flat end cap and unscrew the cap from the muzzle end of the suppressor. If yours wears the brake instead, go to the next step.
steps.prose: BANISH suggests joining the key and the Torx wrench to each other for good with JB Weld or a similar product. That is the two tools only: nothing is ever bonded to the can.
steps.quote: If the flat end cap is installed, use the provided tool key and T-45 Torx wrench, remove the end cap of the suppressor.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: If the brake is fitted: collar loose, then the brake off
steps.action: Loosen the brake's locking collar with the supplied suppressor brake wrench. Then use the tool key and the T-45 Torx wrench to unscrew the brake from the suppressor.
steps.prose: Collar first: the collar is what locks the brake in position, so the brake will fight you until it is loose. The brake's timing is lost when it comes off, and is set again when it goes back on.
steps.quote: If the suppressor brake is installed, use the provided suppressor brake wrench to loosen the locking collar. Use the tool key and T-45 Torx wrench to remove the suppressor brake.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Breach cap off with a 1-inch wrench
steps.action: Put a 1-inch wrench, or an adjustable wrench set snug, on the wrench flats and remove the breach cap.
steps.prose: Breach cap is BANISH's own name and the book does not picture or define it. Turn only a part that has wrench flats. If what your wrench is on does not have them, or will not start, stop and call BANISH.
steps.quote: Using the wrench flats and a 1-inch or adjustable wrench, remove the breach cap.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Twenty-four hour soak
steps.action: Put the whole can and the parts you removed under cleaning solution, or seal the muzzle end and fill the inside, and leave it for 24 hours either way. Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or even dish soap all work. What does not is anything that strips the Cerakote.
steps.prose: The interval is every 50 to 100 rounds. Because the baffles never come out, the soak is what reaches them, so do not cut it short.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50-100 rounds fired.
steps.quote: To clean, submerge the entire suppressor and disassembled suppressor parts in cleaning solution. Or, seal the muzzle end of the suppressor and fill its interior with cleaning solution.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7
steps.warn: Be sure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote finish.

steps.title: Brass brush the blast chamber
steps.action: After the soak, clean the blast chamber, the first chamber inside the mount end of the can, with a brass brush.
steps.prose: Brass is what BANISH names. The blast chamber is the only inside surface it has you brush, so leave the brush out of the baffles.
steps.quote: In both cases, let the suppressor soak for 24 hours. Once soaked, use a brass brush to clean the blast chamber.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Mounting adapter out, and every thread cleaned
steps.action: Take the mounting adapter out and clean all of the threads: the suppressor's own, and the mount's inside and outside threads. Clear out any debris or buildup.
steps.prose: Carbon left in a thread is what stops the mount or the end cap going fully home, and a mount that is not seated points the bore off line.
steps.quote: Remove the mounting adapter and thoroughly clean the threads, removing any debris or buildup. This includes the suppressor’s threads, as well as all internal and external mounting threads.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Solvent out, then let it dry
steps.action: Check that every part is clean and that no excess solvent is left in it. Then let the suppressor dry before anything goes back on.
steps.prose: At the next range session, 10 to 15 clearing rounds blow out whatever the soak loosened.
steps.aside: During the next range session, fire 10-15 “clearing” rounds through the suppressor.
steps.quote: Make sure all parts are clean and excess solvent has been removed.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.7

steps.title: Protect the muzzle while the can is off
steps.action: Whenever the can is off the rifle for storage or transport, protect the barrel's threads and crown with a thread protector or other muzzle device.
steps.prose: A nicked muzzle thread is what starts a can crooked the next time it goes on.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH COMP 6.5 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-9-26"; its upload path is /2026/09/). — WARNING, p.2

deepAbsentReason: The books end at the mount interface, the brake and the flat end cap. On the CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY page (p.7) BANISH states: 'The welded-tubeless BANISH COMP 6.5 SS is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface, suppressor brake, and flat end cap can be removed for cleaning.' The titanium book says the same of the TI on its p.7. Each book prints one cleaning procedure, and all of it (end cap or brake, breach cap, soak, brass brush, threads) is in the routine lane above. This listing therefore has no deep clean.

cleaning.name: INTERIOR
tasks: Whole can and removed parts submerged, or muzzle end sealed and the inside filled, for 24 hours
Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or dish soap
Blast chamber brushed with a brass brush after the soak
⛔ Never a solution that strips the Cerakote finish
⛔ Do not try to remove the baffles: they do not come out

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Mount's inside and outside threads cleaned

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: All parts clean, excess solvent out, suppressor dry
10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session
Thread protector or other muzzle device on the barrel while the can is off

reassembly: All parts clean, free of excess solvent and dry.
Breach cap back on with a 1-inch or adjustable wrench.
Flat end cap, if you run it: start it carefully and do not cross-thread it. If you feel resistance, take it back off and check the threads of both the suppressor and the cap for debris.
Finish the flat end cap with the supplied tool key to 20-25 inch-pounds, or hand tight. Only the 45-degree bevel should show, about 1/32 inch.
Rifle safe and unloaded before the can goes on. Barrel and suppressor threads clean and undamaged.

Direct thread: line the suppressor up with the barrel threads and screw it on until it seats firmly against the shoulder. Do not cross-thread it. Hand tighten only. Any other mount goes on by its own maker's instructions.
Brake, if you run it, goes on after the suppressor is securely on the rifle: loosen its locking collar to the top of the threads, then screw the brake into the suppressor until hand tight.
Set the brake's top and bottom: the top has the larger openings after the first port, and the triangular slot in the front always points to the top.
Tighten the locking collar by hand, then finish with the supplied suppressor brake wrench (the stainless book says until snug).
Refine the brake's alignment and retighten as needed. A bubble level on the flat section of the brake confirms it.
fncheck: With the rifle still unloaded: no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor mount, and nothing blocking the can. ⛔ If there is any gap, do not fire with the suppressor attached. Flat end cap: only the 45-degree bevel shows, about 1/32 inch. Brake: top side up, triangular slot toward the top, collar tight. Check that the can is still tight after the first 5 shots and every 30 after that, once it has cooled or with a cover, and fire 10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session. Damaged or defective: contact BANISH Customer Service before you ship it.
